newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas domestic load factor falls in March.
newsitem.headline: Qantas domestic load factor falls in March.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd's domestic load factor, which measures how full its planes are with paying passengers, fell in the month of March and was lower in the financial year (July-June) to date than a year earlier, Qantas' traffic statistics showed on Wednesday.
Qantas' domestic revenue seat factor (RSF) fell to 76.6 percent in March from 77.9 percent in March 1996 and its year-to-date RSF has fallen to 78.1 percent from 79.5 percent.
Qantas' international RSF however rose to 76.2 percent in March from 70.7 percent a year earlier and year-to-date RSF rose to 72.6 percent from 71.6 percent.
Group RSF rose to 76 percent in March from 71.9 percent in March a year earlier and year-to-date RSF rose to 73.5 percent from 73.0 percent.
Domestic passenger numbers rose to 811,000 in the month of March from 792,000 a year earlier, while year-to-date passenger numbers rose to 7.289 million from 7.084 million.

Group passenger numbers rose to 1.590 million in March from 1.485 million in March 1996, while year-to-date group passenger numbers rose to 14.099 million from 13.242 million over the same period in 1995/96.
Shares in Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, were up four cents at A$2.76 at 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT).
Qantas' major domestic competitor, Ansett Australia, does not issue monthly traffic statistics.
Ansett Australia is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
